title: Authorised push payment: victim tricked into paying a fake account
summary: A customer received a convincing call claiming to be from their bank's fraud team and was persuaded to move their savings to a 'safe account'. The customer authorised the payment themselves, from their own trusted device.
signals: this payment empties the sender's account completely
the money is going to a receiver never used before
the amount is far above what is normal for this customer
resolution: Customer confirmed the payment when challenged, because they believed the caller. Funds were lost. Case is retained as a reminder of the limits of OTP.
lesson: OTP confirms that the account holder approved a payment — not that the payment is safe. A trusted device proves identity, never intent. This is the one case where the step-up path fails by design.
